newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares gain 0.91pct on buoyant bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares gain 0.91pct on buoyant bank shares.

text.p: Shares in the Athens bourse firmed 0.91 percent on Monday in active trading focused on select bank and industrial blue chips shares.
Market watchers said sentiment was bullish for the market's short-term prospects with foreign buying evident in large caps.
"We're experiencing substantial buying interest from foreign institutionals in private sector banks and industrial large caps." said Thanos Trikatzis, broker with Hermes Securities.
"Private banks are leading this rally, but public sector credit institutions should be expected to follow suit," he added.
Turnover is rising steadily, despite entering a pre-Easter phase of idleness.
"Interest in telecoms-related stocks is picking up too, as Intracom is headed for a sizeable rights issue in the coming months," he added.
The Athens share index ended 0.91 percent or 12.97 points higher at 1,441.04, from Friday's 1,428.07. The index opened up at 1,432.86 and reached an intra-day high of 1,447.56 shortly after.

Turnover rose to 15.4 billion drachmas on volume of 4.2 million shares. Alpha Credit was the day's most heavily traded stock, with turnover of 3.1 billion drachmas, including a block trade of 59,000 shares at 19,650.
Other block trades included Hellenic Bottling, 80,000 shares at 9,000, and construction firm Proodeftiki, 100,000 shares at 1,880 drachmas.
Decliners led advancers 115 to 92 with 34 issues unchanged on 241 traded.
Banks led the market advance with a 1.78 percent rise, mostly attributed to Alpha Credit's 4.73 percent jump to 19,690 drachmas, on rumours of substantially improved first quarter profit.
Industrials were up 0.64 percent, lifted mostly by Hellenic Bottling's 2.04 percent appreciation to 8,985 drachmas and Chipita which closed up 495 drachmas.
Construction lost 2.15 percent as investor interest remains slack in the sector.
